blocking_findings.problem: Grok is described as an established Read-only, no-web, no-subagent control. This session is Grok 4.7 on Windows 11/PowerShell and still exposes file tools, MCP lookup/call, and skill entrypoints for browser, computer-use, web research, and subagent-style workflows. The plan states that Antigravity's broad tools are not hard isolation, but it does not apply that standard to Grok. Prompt text does not enforce those denials, so a packet could mutate files or reach the network despite section 6.
blocking_findings.recommended_change: Dispatch Grok only with an explicit tool allowlist: read-only file access; deny shell, write, web, MCP, browser, computer-use, and subagents. Record the actual tool list, requested model grok-4.7, resolved model, and effort. If the CLI cannot deny those tools, send no secret-adjacent or frozen-input packets and keep accepting stdout proposals only.

nonblocking_findings.problem: Grok's primary role is one exact diff and one risk, while section 4 says Codex must not rebuild a sound artifact and prefers usable patches. A prose-only finding makes Codex re-derive the fix.
nonblocking_findings.recommended_change: For a local ownership, lifecycle, or coupling defect, require one applicable hunk plus the single risk. Keep ABI/kernel work on a reviewed contract; do not widen the review to the whole tree.

nonblocking_findings.problem: The 180-240s Grok cap is only a suggestion, but a single ABI or calling-convention question on Windows can exceed it if the packet includes headers and toolchain facts. Low effort matches a narrow review, not a short clock.
nonblocking_findings.recommended_change: Set the cap from the one deliverable after the packet is fixed. Record timeout separately from an empty or invalid artifact. Do not treat grok-4.7-build-fast as a latency or quality fallback without a new qualified trial.

model_role_advice: Keep grok-4.7 at low effort for one focused defect or ownership/lifecycle/coupling review. Do not use it as coverage primary or as the test author for an implementation it wrote.
grok-4.7-build-fast, 4.6, and 4.5 stay unqualified candidates. This round does not confirm CLI 1.0.52 or the authenticated catalog; those remain prior audit claims.
